content:
AIYANA BROOKS-TAN
Junior Frontend / Full-Stack Developer
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
github.com/aiyana-bt-example | aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Junior developer with hands-on experience building React and TypeScript applications, accessible user interfaces, and a Node.js/Express API backed by PostgreSQL through academic and personal projects. Experienced with automated testing using Jest and React Testing Library, and with documenting reusable components in Storybook. Particularly interested in building accessible, user-focused web experiences.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1; keyboard and screen-reader accessibility

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS; deployed it on Vercel.
- Made small updates to two WordPress websites.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked with the web team on the company’s React news site.
- Fixed accessibility issues across 20+ components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels.
- Built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery and documented it with Storybook stories.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Liffey Institute of Technology | Spring 2025
- Helped approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development lab sessions.

Barista (Part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025

SELECTED PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app showing tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Developed the React and TypeScript frontend, plus a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs.
- Used PostgreSQL to store users’ favourite locations; tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers.
- Achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 and a project grade of 82% (First Class); demonstrated the project at the college showcase.
- Technologies: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Chart.js, Jest.

Yoga Studio Booking Site | Freelance Project | 2025
- Created marketing pages and a class timetable, with booking requests sent by email.
- Used Next.js static generation and Tailwind CSS; content is managed in Markdown files and the site is deployed on Vercel.

Accessible Gallery Component | Harbourline Media | 2024
- Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages.
- Technologies: React, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library.

Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a student web app that matched classmates for study sessions.
- Collaborated in a team of four; other team members developed the API and database.
- Technologies: React, JavaScript, Firebase Authentication.

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
First Class Honours
- Final-year project: “Tidewatch” – accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers.
- Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms.

ADDITIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS
- Second place, student hackathon (2024): worked in a three-person team to build a transit delay notifier in 24 hours; developed the frontend.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and appropriately targeted toward a junior React/TypeScript role. It provides credible evidence through quantified accessibility work, named technologies, project outcomes, testing tools, and a strong First Class degree. The combination of internship, freelance work, teaching assistance, and relevant projects gives the document good substance. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected when cross-referenced with the original candidate information. The main content limitation is that the CV does not clearly distinguish professional experience from academic and personal project experience, which matters for this role's 2+ years professional-experience requirement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The layout uses conventional section headings, standard text, clear date ranges, and ATS-friendly keyword placement. Strong matching terms include React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, WCAG 2.1, accessibility, and Vercel. The document should parse reliably and has a moderate-to-high AI screening probability for junior frontend/full-stack searches. Strict screening may reduce the match because it does not contain explicit terms for end-to-end testing, OWASP Top 10, web security fundamentals, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, GDPR, Docker, AWS, or NestJS. These are candidate gaps rather than terms that should be added without supporting evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the role's React/TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Next.js, wellness-related, Storybook, and unit-testing requirements. Tidewatch is particularly relevant because it demonstrates an end-to-end application, an API, SQL storage, third-party API integration, screen-reader testing, and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The yoga-studio booking project provides relevant wellness and booking-domain context. The teaching assistant experience also supports the role's mentoring preference. The principal gap is the requirement for 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript web-application experience: the material shows an internship and freelance work, but not two years of professional experience. End-to-end testing, web-security fundamentals, health-data privacy, Docker/AWS, German/Croatian, and analytics/A/B testing are also not supported by the candidate material. The CV should not imply these capabilities. Overall, it is a strong junior-level match but not a complete match for the stated must-have profile.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the Professional Summary, change “Experienced with automated testing using Jest and React Testing Library” to “Experienced with automated unit testing using Jest and React Testing Library.” This is more precise because the CV documents unit tests but does not document integration or end-to-end testing.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the Professional Summary, make the professional-versus-project scope explicit by changing the opening to: “Junior developer with professional internship and freelance experience, plus academic and personal projects, building React and TypeScript applications...” This preserves the strong positioning while avoiding any implication that the candidate already has 2+ years of professional experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 3 — In the Technical Skills section, change “Testing and tools” to “Testing, version control and tools” and retain “Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma.” This makes the Git-based workflow keyword easier for ATS systems to identify without adding unsupported experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 4 — In the Experience section under “Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance),” change “Built a booking website...” to “Built and deployed a booking website...” because deployment on Vercel is already supported by the existing bullet and this presents the delivery responsibility more clearly.
